name: GrapeLeads
summary: Lead-finding for web developers and agencies — surfaces local businesses without websites from Google Maps, with contact details, on signup credits.
best_for: web developers, designers and agencies prospecting local businesses that do not have a website yet — surfaced from Google Maps with contact details
skip_if: you sell to companies that already have an online presence, or you want transparent pricing before creating an account
honest_knock: You are billed per result, not per usable lead: one credit opens the search and one more is charged for every business it returns, so a broad filter burns credits whether or not the results are worth calling. The packs are small enough that this is cheap to test ($28 for 50 credits) but it is the wrong shape if you want volume prospecting at a predictable monthly cost — there is no subscription at all. The site also still 404s its own /pricing link while the real list sits at /buy-credits/, which is an odd look for a tool sold to web professionals. And the niche (Google-Maps businesses without websites) is the real product: judge the data on one pack before you go further.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-12, read on their own buy-credits page; every amount unchanged since 12 August) Pay-as-you-go credit packs, bought once rather than subscribed to: Freelancer $28 for 50 credits ($0.56 each), Startup $55 for 100 credits ($0.54) and Agency $127 for 250 credits ($0.51). Bulk pricing is on request and signing up gives 20 free credits. Credits measure work, not leads: one credit starts a search and one more is charged for every filtered result, so a search that returns 20 matching businesses costs 21 credits. The vendor also states that unused credits carry a 50% bonus when its 2.0 app ships. Mind the URL — the price list lives at /buy-credits/ while the /pricing link 404s, which is how we had this down as unpriced until now. One rounding note: the page prints $0.54 per credit for the Startup pack, but $55 for 100 credits is $0.55 — their own figure is a cent optimistic.
